findings.detail: A price and upgrade CTA is the visually primary action on a waitlist receipt, before the person has seen anything built from their data.
A synthetic test identity is rendered to the user as their email address.
A route path is shown as content and leaks into a button label.

Pen p1IJJ is a bare left-aligned 'jov.ie/avery is yours.' headline with one paragraph and one quiet status line; the run uses a different, weaker composition that buries the handle claim in body text and adds a list and CTAs.
Icon tile plus a wrapper card around a lone receipt, neither of which exists in Pen.
Title Case button label, on top of a stacked title, paragraph, three-item list and button row.
Numbered instruction list in engineering-ticket voice with an em dash where one sentence would do.
No single focal point: the handle claim competes with a title, list and two actions, and the small card sits lost in dead space.
The handle carries an unexplained numeric suffix, which reads as a silent change from the name the person chose (only one frame, so the prior handle can't be confirmed here).

'Start Pro ($12)' shows a price with no billing period (one-time? per month? per year?) and no description of what Pro gets you. It's also the primary, highlighted button on a 'you're on the waitlist' receipt. The page says 'wait for access', but the main action is 'pay now'. The user can't tell whether paying skips the waitlist or what the $12 is for.

Step 1 shows an internal synthetic test address ('browse-ready+synthetic-prodcert-wlcert1029a@jov.ie') and splits it across two lines at a hyphen. A real user's email this long would wrap just as badly, and the leaked fixture makes the screen look like a test build.
The intro promises 'we'll email you the moment your spot opens', but step 2 says 'a few days once capacity opens — not instant'. The two timing messages say different things and are both vague.

'Resume At Start' is awkward Title Case, and it repeats step 3 (which already exposes the raw '/start' route path to the user). The arrow sits right up against the text with no gap. The label doesn't say what the user is resuming.
Step 3's 'or the waitlist page; your context stays attached to this request' is jargon ('context', 'request'). It has no link and doesn't say where the waitlist page is.
Pipeline vocabulary (source: enrichment) is printed as user-facing content under the profile preview.
The agent reply names the internal enrichment pipeline to the user.
The preview shows a placeholder handle after the artist was matched, when Pen shows the real proposed handle.
The agent tells the person to do a task it could do itself: it proposes no handle and asks nothing, so the conversation stalls.
Three clipped sentences in stiff system voice that read like a log line, not a person talking.
Uses an em dash, a banned slop tell, in user-facing copy.
About two-thirds of the chat column is dead space with no heading, profile-ready summary or next question.
Same chat-plus-preview split as Pen R6As7U, but with the hierarchy and component set stripped out, so it reads as a debug harness rather than the designed chat.
An icon sits in a bordered tile, where Pen uses a bare mark.
Title Case controls and an all-caps label break the sentence-case rule.
The assistant reply exposes internal pipeline wording to the user: "Enrichment shows 201 Spotify followers." "Enrichment" is a backend term. It reads like a debug log, not a product message.
The caption under the preview says "(source: enrichment)", which leaks the same internal data-source label into the UI. It also repeats the follower count that's already in the chat.
The message says "Claim a handle next" but gives no button, handle field, or suggested handle. The only option is the empty free-text composer, so the next step is a dead end.
The preview shows the placeholder "jov.ie/your-handle" as if it were real profile content. It looks unfinished, and the app could have suggested a real handle based on the artist name.
The assistant message is small, plain text with no avatar, name, or bubble. It looks like a stray log line rather than a reply, and the 201-follower stat sounds faintly negative with no context.
The pasted Spotify URL is shown raw in the user bubble. It isn't turned into a recognizable artist chip and looks clipped at the right edge.
The top of the phone preview is malformed. The Spotify badge sits on the bezel corner, overlapping the frame, and the purple gradient band at the top looks like a cropped or misaligned frame.
Most of the chat column is empty dead space, with a single short line at the top and the composer far below. The layout feels unbalanced and unfinished.
Pipeline provenance text ("source: enrichment") appears as user-facing copy.
The agent's reply uses the word "Enrichment" and reads like a pipeline log.
A synthetic cert-run identity is on screen, so this recording can't be shown to a person.
Raw state and enum values (lowercase "artist", "Review") are shown as a status line.
The agent ignores both handles the user typed and repeats the same canned line.
The chat and the live preview show two different handles in the same frame.
The handle changes from unmarked to unmarked1 and nothing explains why (for example that @unmarked is taken).
The copy has an em dash, a verbatim repeat, filler justification and internal routing language.
It keeps Pen's two-pane idea but drops most of R6As7U's hierarchy and components, so it reads like a debug harness.
The top actions use Title Case.
The icon sits in a bordered tile; Pen shows a bare mark in that spot.
The all-caps chip repeats what the panel already makes obvious.
Vertical rhythm is uneven and the chat's left edge doesn't line up with the composer.

The assistant ignored the handle the user typed. The user sent 'wlcert1029a' and Jovie answered 'Claiming @unmarked for you', a handle the user never asked for. The user's input gets silently overridden.

The same reply appears twice. After the user sent 'unmarked1', Jovie repeated its earlier line word for word, still claiming '@unmarked'. That doesn't match what the user typed or the jov.ie/unmarked1 shown in the preview. It reads like a stuck bot.

Jovie asks how big the user's audience is right after it said it found 201 Spotify followers. Asking for something it already knows makes the 'qualify' step feel scripted and makes the user wonder why it's asking.
Internal pipeline wording shows up in user-facing copy: 'Enrichment shows 201 Spotify followers.' A user doesn't know what 'enrichment' means.
Debug or metadata text sits under the preview: 'Draft · artist · Review' and '201 Spotify followers (source: enrichment)'. It looks like leftover developer labels, not finished UI.
'Confirmed handle @unmarked1' appears in a user-style bubble, as if the user said it. A system confirmation dressed up as the user's own message is confusing.
'Claiming… checking it now' never resolves. No message says whether the handle was available or taken, so the user can't tell which handle they actually got.
The agent ignores both handles the person typed and repeats the same reply, so the only button is disabled and there is no working way forward.
The screen says the handle is taken, that it is being claimed, and that it is the live URL, all at once.
Pipeline vocabulary is printed as user-facing copy.
The agent reply leaks the word 'Enrichment' and reads like a pipeline log.
Internal record status and type labels are shown as a caption.
The handle the person chose is not carried into the live preview.
The reply uses an em dash, adds filler explanation and repeats word for word.
The person has to fix the handle in a form widget while the conversation ignores what they type.
The primary action is Title Case and disabled by default.
The top-bar labels are Title Case.
The icon sits in a bordered circular tile.
The inline widget is indented off the chat column's shared left edge.
Chat beside a live profile is kept, but the shell, the hierarchy and the agent identity from Pen R6As7U are missing.
The user typed the handle "wlcert1029a", but the assistant replies "Claiming @unmarked for you". It ignores what the user typed and tries to claim a different handle.

The user then typed the suggested handle "unmarked1", and the assistant repeats the exact same "Claiming @unmarked…" message word for word. It ignores the input a second time, so the flow is stuck in a loop and the user can't move forward.

The claim card is contradictory. It says @unmarked is not available, yet the input still holds @unmarked instead of the suggested @unmarked1. The Confirm Handle button looks disabled, and nothing reflects the handles the user actually typed. The card was also never updated after the second attempt.
The live preview shows the URL jov.ie/unmarked, which the card just said is unavailable. The preview is showing a link the user can't get.
Internal jargon is shown to the user: "Enrichment shows 201 Spotify followers". "Enrichment" is a pipeline term, not product copy.
The text under the preview, "201 Spotify followers (source: enrichment)", shows internal data-source labels. It reads like debug output.
"Draft · artist · Review" is an unclear status line with inconsistent capitalization ("artist" is lowercase). It's not obvious whether "Review" is a label or a link.
The Spotify URL message bubble is cut off by the top edge of the chat area, so its text is partly hidden.
The dev toolbar, with environment and version labels and internal tools like Unwaitlist and Sync Clerk, is part of the captured frame.
The conversations list failed to load, and the user sees that failure in the sidebar of the main shell.
An 'unavailable' message gets cut off mid-word, and its only way forward is a bare retry glyph.
The inbox says it is clear even though the data behind it failed to load, so the two states contradict each other and the empty state can't be trusted.
Every label and button in the main pane uses Title Case instead of sentence case.
A small centered focal point is lost in a huge dead canvas, and 'Add Notes' and the tabs compete with the one action.
The sidebar footer elements collide and clip each other instead of stacking.
The agent shows no proposal, completed work or next move, so the person faces a blank prompt.
The orphaned '+' row and the loose header icons don't share a grid with the nav list below.
The header title doesn't match the selected nav item.
The user avatar overlaps the 'Development' badge and cuts it off ('lopment'). A truncated name ('Dan…') shows behind the What's New card. The sidebar footer is visibly broken.
Under 'Today', the sidebar shows an error, 'Conversations unavaila…', with the text cut off and only a retry icon. The error is truncated, unexplained and looks broken.
The main panel says 'Your Inbox Is Clear' while the sidebar says conversations failed to load. The empty state may be hiding a load error and giving the user false reassurance.
'Add Notes' floats alone between the tabs and the empty state. It has no context, no button styling and no clear purpose.
The page header says 'Home', but the selected nav item says 'Inbox'. The page names don't match.
The 'Start A Chat' button sits right under the heading with almost no gap. The empty state has no supporting line and feels cramped and unfinished.
Labels use forced Title Case ('Done For You', 'Your Inbox Is Clear', 'Start A Chat'), which reads stiff and odd for sentence-style copy.
The internal dev toolbar, with build version, breakpoint and admin actions, is captured as part of the product frame.
A test fixture identity shows up as the artist name on every row.
Chat titles start with test-run ids, which is pipeline data shown as content.
The account avatar collides with the What's new card and the dev badge, so the sidebar footer looks broken.
Column widths go to a redundant value and truncate the one column that could inform, and an all-empty Length column adds nothing.
Title Case labels and a crowded header row of quiet controls weaken the Linear-precision header.
This frame falls short of the shell's premium-density bar on data, chrome and column polish, even though the layout regions are right.

The user's avatar overlaps the bottom-left corner. It covers the 'Development' env badge, which is clipped to 'lopment', and it sits on the edge of the What's new card. Behind the card there is a half-hidden, cut-off line of text ('Daniel M…'). The sidebar footer stacking is broken.
Every row in the Type column is truncated to 'Sin…'. The column is too narrow to show a one-word value like 'Single', and the Length column next to it has spare room.
The Artist column shows 'Dogfood Fixture High Reach' on every row. Test-fixture naming is leaking into the UI. It reads as fake data, and it repeats the same value on all 10 rows.
The Length column is all em dashes. A whole column with no data looks unfinished. It should be filled in or hidden.

The recent chats list shows internal test titles ('e2-30900 Thanks. …', 'e1-36867 In one se…') and two identical, truncated 'Generate a playlist …' entries. The titles can't be told apart and look like debug data.
'YouTube Ledger' is plain text sitting next to the Add button. It isn't clear whether it is a button, a label, or a source filter.
The toolbar is crowded with unlabeled icons: sort, columns, and three view-mode toggles. The column/layout icon next to the view switcher looks redundant.
The row status icons mix a green half-filled circle, an empty circle, and grey checks, with no legend or tooltip. Their meaning isn't clear to a first-time user.
'10 of 10 Items' capitalizes 'Items' mid-sentence, which doesn't match the sentence case used elsewhere.
There is a lone '+' in the sidebar with no label or context, so it's unclear what it creates.
Test-run ids show up as chat history titles in the main nav, where a person would read them.
Internal dev tools and environment labels sit across the bottom of the captured frame.
An unavailable banner with no next step sits above an empty table, and it has nothing to do with a person's audience.
The account avatar, the What's new toast and the user row overlap and clip each other in the bottom of the sidebar.
The empty state is a lone bordered card inside a table that already gives it a frame, so it reads as a box inside a box.
The same label repeats across three nav layers, and a fourth filter row sits under them before any content.
The heading, a button and a column header use Title Case.
A small empty state is lost in a mostly empty page under table headers that have no rows.
Generic advice in a stiff system voice, with an unbacked claim about "most creators".

A full-width error banner, 'AI crawler analytics temporarily unavailable.', is the first thing on the page. It's above an empty table, has no retry, no timestamp and no explanation, and it's about a feature the user never asked for. On a first visit the page looks broken.

The user avatar in the bottom-left overlaps the 'What's new' card and covers both the 'Development' badge and the account name below it, which is cut off to an unreadable 'Paul M…'. Layered elements are colliding.

The recent chats list shows test or seed junk ('e2-30900 Thanks…', 'e1-36867 In one se…') plus two identical 'Generate a playlist…' entries on the same date. All titles are truncated so they can't be told apart, which looks unfinished.

The empty state is mixed up with the table. Column headers (State, Alerts, Engagement, Last Seen with an active sort arrow, Action) sit over zero rows, and a boxed card floats underneath them. The filter and export icons stay enabled with nothing to filter or export. It should be one empty state, without the dead table chrome.

The labels repeat themselves: the page is titled 'Audience', the sidebar item is 'Audience', and the selected sub-tab is also 'Audience', sitting next to Contacts and Insights. The way the views are organized isn't clear.
The two buttons use different capitalization: 'Copy profile link' is sentence case and 'Learn About Audience' is title case. The second action also looks like plain text, not a link or button.

The empty-state copy is clumsy and makes an unsupported claim. 'Most creators get their first audience member by sharing on X or IG bio' reads badly ('on … IG bio') and comes across as a made-up statistic.
The internal dev toolbar, with environment, breakpoint and admin tools, runs across the bottom of a frame a person is meant to see.
The chat history shows test fixture ids and leftover eval prompts as the person's own chats.
The sidebar footer elements collide: the avatar, card and badge overlap and the text underneath is cut off, so it looks broken.
Most of the viewport is dead space around a small focal element, and two buttons compete for the one action.
A single message sits in a bordered wrapper card floating in empty space.
The heading and both buttons use Title Case where sentence case is required.
Generic AI-product filler that could describe any analytics tool and says nothing specific to this person.
The agent waits for a button press instead of producing insights on its own, so nothing is taking shape.
Nine filters are shown with nothing to filter, so none of them can help.
No Pen reference is registered, but the screen falls well short of the premium, dense entity-first shell bar.

The avatar overlaps the bottom of the sidebar. It covers the 'Development' environment badge (only 'lopment' is visible) and clips a line of text under the What's new card, which shows as half-cut glyphs.
The What's new card collides with the sidebar footer. Text behind or below it (something like 'Rename…') is cut off, so the stack looks broken.

The recent chats list shows raw test titles ('e2-30900 Thanks…', 'e1-36867 In one se…') and two identical truncated 'Generate a playlist …' rows. It looks like seeded junk data and makes the product feel untrustworthy.
A lone 'No Insights Yet' card floats in a huge empty canvas. The page shows no audience data, preview, or skeleton, so it reads as an unfinished dead-end empty state, not a useful Audience page.
Nine filter tabs (Geographic, Growth, Revenue, Tour, …) are active even though there is no data. Every tab filters nothing, which promises content that doesn't exist.
'Share Profile' is an odd secondary action inside an 'insights' empty state. It isn't related to generating insights, and its plain-text style makes it read like a label, not a button.
The copy is generic and uses Title Case ('No Insights Yet', 'AI-powered insights to discover actionable trends'). This is filler marketing language that doesn't say what the user will get.
The page title 'Audience' is tiny and doesn't match the content, which is entirely about 'Insights'. The user can't tell which page they are on.
The unlabeled sparkle icon at the far top right has no visible meaning or tooltip. It sits far away from the tabs it presumably relates to.
It is a decision card with no way to approve, choose an alternative or reply, so the next step is a dead end.
Raw Stripe price ids and a database row count are shown as content.
The body uses an em dash and reads like a pasted ops ticket full of parentheticals, not a decision written for a person.
Nothing is the focal point: the recommendation and the alternatives are the same grey prose, and there is no action to take.
Three stacked text layers with a long grey body make the actual ask hard to scan.

This card asks for a pricing decision, but there's no way to answer it. There are no Approve, Reject or Choose buttons, and nothing to pick the proposal or an alternative. It looks like a read-only card in an inbox that's supposed to be actionable.
Raw Stripe price IDs (price_1TG8IWAAI1NrDqJSGT7nzvRF and three more) are pasted into the body copy. That's implementation detail, hard to read, and makes the card look like an unedited agent dump.

The body is one dense wall of text. The proposal, the gating condition, grandfathering, the archive actions and the default change all run together with no structure, so you can't see what you're approving at a glance.
The alternatives are a sentence of plain text, not separate options you can select. That makes it unclear how to pick 'keep $12' or 'jump to $29' instead of the main proposal.
The body text is low-contrast gray on near-black, which makes long text tiring to read and makes the important numbers recede.
Internal jargon leaks into the copy: 'production delivery receipt (today: 0 rows ever)' reads like a database note, not language for the person making the decision.
The heading repeats the body almost word for word. It isn't a short summary, so the card says the same thing twice.
There's no metadata: no date, source, status or count. The 'Inbox' header shows a single item with no context, and the dim Refresh button floats on its own with weak affordance.
Our text sits on lettered artwork and the busy jacket pattern, so the title appears twice and the art's own type gets covered.
With no Pen to match, this still falls short of the bar: the cover is cropped and framed by mismatched bands instead of shown whole as the hero.
The primary button label breaks the sentence-case rule. The release title itself is a proper name, so it is not counted.
All caps is used as default styling, and the separator spacing is off.
Two clipped fragments that read like an engineering note and do not say what gets switched or remembered.
The focal action is clear, but the lower third is dead space with nothing intentional in it.
The icons are in bordered circle tiles rather than bare.
The cover art isn't full-bleed. It sits in a box with the art's white border and dark bars on both sides, so it looks like a letterboxed thumbnail instead of a cinematic hero.
The text printed on the artwork ("NEVER SAY A WORD") is clipped at the top edge of the screen and runs under the back and menu buttons.

The title and artist overlay sits on top of the artwork's own printed text. The cover's lower text shows through behind "Tim White", and the title repeats what is already on the cover, so the overlay looks cluttered.
The hero ends in a hard horizontal cut, with no gradient fade into the dark page, so the photo looks pasted on.
The main button says "Stream Now" but doesn't name the service. Spotify is shown only by its small icon, while the services around it (Deezer, Apple Music) are named in text.
Deezer and Apple Music appear as faded floating rows above and below the button. They look disabled, and it isn't clear they are options in a swipeable picker.
The helper text "Swipe to switch. Always remembered." is vague. It doesn't say what gets switched or remembered, and it's a workaround for a picker that doesn't explain itself.
About 30% of the screen is empty dark space between the helper text and the footer. The layout feels unfinished and top-heavy.
Footer spacing is off: "·REPORT" has no space after the dot. The bare all-caps "REPORT" link also reads as alarming next to the branding.
Our title sits on top of lettered cover art, so the text overlaps text and the cover's own title is duplicated and cropped.
The step promises a blurred cover behind text, but it shows a cropped, sharp, bordered cover with a hard cut, which is weaker than the premium release-hero bar.
The primary button is in Title Case instead of sentence case. The screen judge missed this.
The all-caps tracked footer is a default styling move and reads below the type scale.
The action cluster floats mid-screen with a large dead region under it and nothing intentional filling it.
Reads like a stiff two-fragment slogan. It explains the mechanism instead of helping the person choose a service.
The icons are boxed in filled circular tiles. A scrim over the photo makes this partly defensible, so it is minor.
The separator is optically off-center between the two footer items.

The hero crops the cover art badly. The art's own white frame shows on both sides, its printed title 'NEVER SAY A WORD' is cut off at the top edge, and leftover cover text peeks out at the bottom. It looks like a scaled-down cover pasted into the page, not a full-bleed hero.

The artwork ends in a hard horizontal edge around a third of the way down, with no fade into the dark background. Faint, unreadable text from the cover sits right at that edge. It looks broken or unfinished.

The page shows the cover title twice: once printed on the art and again as the large white 'Never Say A Word' overlay. The overlay also sits on top of the subject's body and the art's white frame, so the hero looks cluttered.

The provider picker is confusing. The faded Deezer and Apple Music rows above and below the main button look disabled, not like swipeable choices. The main button says 'Stream Now' and only a small icon shows it's Spotify, and 'Swipe to switch. Always remembered.' doesn't say what is being remembered.
About a third of the screen between the helper text and the footer is empty dark space, so the page feels sparse and unfinished. There's no release info, other links or artist context.
The footer spacing is off: '·REPORT' has no space after the dot but a large gap before it. 'Report' is also a strange action to put next to the brand mark.
The page calls the profile verified and unclaimed at the same moment, so a visitor can't tell which state is true.
The release credit doesn't match the artist printed on the artwork, so the catalog match looks wrong and hurts trust.
Two listen actions repeat each other, and two white primary pills compete, so the page has no single action. The bottom third is empty apart from a spinner.
The button label is Title Case, not sentence case.
A spinner is still showing on a page that otherwise looks loaded, so it reads as stuck loading.
Stiff system copy that reads like an engineering rule, shown to every visitor and not only the artist.
A blue verified checkmark sits on the avatar, but the banner right above says the profile is unclaimed. A profile can't be both verified and unclaimed, so visitors have no reason to trust either.
The cover art says 'TIM WHITE', but the release is credited to 'Unfazed'. The artist name and the artwork don't agree, so it looks like the wrong release or bad data.

There are two listen buttons: 'Listen' under the profile and 'Listen now' under the release. They look different, and the secondary white pill stands out more than the dark main button. It's unclear which one is the main action.
A loading spinner is stuck at the bottom of the page, so the page looks like it never finished loading.
The unclaimed banner runs to two lines and its icon is tiny and hard to read. It isn't aligned with the content grid, so it looks patched in rather than designed.
The '...' overflow menu sits below the nav baseline and outside the content width. It looks misplaced and isn't aligned with the tabs.
A debug state readout is shown to the user on a public release surface.
Roughly 70% of the viewport is empty, and with no cover art, title or artist the small dial has no context: the user can't tell what they are about to stream.
The primary button label is in Title Case.
The third option fades to a contrast level that is barely readable, so the user can't tell it is tappable.
Debug overlay is left in the build: green monospace text 'selected: spotify / pos: 0' in the bottom-left corner. It makes the screen look unfinished and untrustworthy.
About 70% of the screen below the dial is empty dark space. The page shows no artist, artwork, release title, or other context, so a first-time user can't tell what 'Stream Now' will play.

The primary CTA says 'Stream Now' with only a small Spotify glyph and never names Spotify, while the other options are labeled 'Apple Music' and 'Deezer'. The labeling is inconsistent, and users can't be sure where the button takes them.
The 'Deezer' option is faded to very low contrast against the dark background, so it's hard to read and looks disabled rather than like a selectable item further down the dial.
Our title sits on lettered cover art, so the release name shows up twice and our copy lands on top of the artwork's copy.
This step is meant to be a square cover with the title below, but the frame is a cropped full-bleed hero, so the artwork is mangled and there's a stray text fragment under it.
The primary button is in Title Case; the release title is a proper name and is fine.
The footer uses all caps as a default style move.
The service rows don't share an icon column, and the footer separator is spaced unevenly.
It's cryptic system voice: it doesn't say what gets switched or what gets remembered.
The faded carousel rows read like stray secondary links and the lower fifth of the screen sits empty, but the single primary action is still clear, so this isn't a major issue.
The square cover art is cropped badly in the hero. The title printed on the artwork ('NEVER SAY A WORD') is cut off at the top edge, right behind the status/nav area.
The bottom of the artwork ends in a hard edge and leaves ghost text behind: the 'TIM WHITE' printed on the cover peeks out half-hidden under the overlay title block. It looks broken.
The artwork doesn't fill the hero. Light grey/white letterbox strips show along the left and right edges and the top, so the image looks pasted in instead of full-bleed.
The title and artist appear twice: once as the overlay text 'Never Say A Word / Tim White' and again printed on the cover art itself. That's redundant and cluttered.

The main CTA says 'Stream Now' with only a Spotify glyph. It never names the service, so a first-time user can't tell where it goes. The faded Deezer/Apple Music rows above and below read as disabled, not as alternatives to pick.
'Swipe to switch. Always remembered.' is cryptic copy. It's unclear what you swipe, which direction, and what gets remembered.
There's a large dead empty area between the helper text and the footer, so the lower half feels unfinished and unbalanced.
The footer spacing is inconsistent ('JOVIE ·REPORT': no space after the dot). 'REPORT' is vague and sits right next to the branding.
An internal step label and a route path with a query string show at the top of the screen. The text is also about 10px, under the 12px floor, and contains an em dash.
The person has claimed a handle and answered a question, but their page is not taking shape anywhere, so the answers produce no visible result.
The messages sit at the top and leave about 40% of the viewport empty above the composer, so the current question and its answer chip end up far apart.
The speakers are told apart only by a small difference in fill, so the conversation reads as one undifferentiated stack.
The flattering opener and the explanation of the process are filler before the actual question.
A secondary control is drawn as a heavy filled tile that competes with the send button, and it is styled differently from the bare mic.
Nothing shows where to type a different answer from the chip, and send looks enabled with an empty input.

User and assistant messages look almost the same. Every bubble is left-aligned with nearly the same dark fill and the same width behavior, so you can't easily tell 'I want to claim…' and 'Product designer…' (the user) from Jovie's replies. User messages should be right-aligned or styled clearly differently.
A design annotation shows in the UI: '1 · Qualify chat — /start?handle=avery' is a frame label or route note, not product copy. It looks unfinished and leaks an internal URL.

The composer has no visible text input or placeholder. There is only a '+' button, a mic and a send arrow on empty space, so it isn't clear where to type. The send button is also bright white (looks enabled) even though the input is empty.

A lone white 'Instagram and my site ↗' pill floats above the composer. It's unclear whether it's a suggested reply, a draft, or a link (the ↗ suggests it opens something external). A single suggestion chip also reads like a leading answer, not a choice.
A large dead area sits between the last question and the composer. The conversation is crammed at the top while half the screen stays empty, so it feels sparse and unbalanced.
The mic icon is tiny and low-contrast next to the strong white send button, so it's easy to miss and looks disabled.
The designer's step id and the internal ICP qualification label sit on screen as the receipt's eyebrow, which tells the person they were sorted out as not a fit.
About three quarters of the viewport is empty, so a small text block floats at the top with nothing intentional below it.
The only accent-colored text looks like a link but does nothing, and the receipt gives no next step besides waiting.
The copy uses cohort, waves and position mechanics, which reads like an ops note, and it implies a queue position it never shows.
The screen says "your name and profile are reserved" but shows neither, which falls below the living-canvas bar for the claim flow.
The eyebrow is below 12px and adds a fourth type layer (eyebrow, title, body, status) to a single message.

An internal design annotation is showing as page copy: "3a · Reserved — waitlisted or not ICP yet". It exposes internal jargon (ICP, the state number) and tells the user they may have been judged not to fit the target customer.
About 75% of the screen is empty. There's no next step: no CTA, no way to share or preview the profile, no link back, no logo or nav. The flow just stops, which makes it look unfinished.

"Position rises as we clear this cohort's feedback" is internal-ops language and doesn't make sense to a user. They're told about a position but never shown what it is. It's also styled in link blue but doesn't appear to be clickable.
The headline says the name "is yours", but the body says the profile is only reserved and access is waitlisted. The mixed message weakens trust.
The only image supplied is the Pen reference itself, with a design-annotation caption (step index, internal name, em dash) that is not user-facing copy and would be internal leakage if it shipped.

Internal design-board annotation is baked into the frame: the '0 · Proof profile — jov.ie/tim on a phone' label and the 'Claim yours, right above the dock.' headline read as notes to the team, not product copy. Notes like this on the page make it look unfinished and cost trust. The headline also wraps to leave 'dock.' as an orphan.

The Listen card has stray gradient artifacts. A purple wedge is clipped hard at the top-right, and a lavender sliver sticks out at the bottom-left below the card's content. They look like rendering glitches, not intentional lighting.

The album art looks like a cropped screenshot. It has a thick white border, and thin strips of tiny, unreadable text show along its top and bottom edges. It's also small for the card, which leaves big empty gutters on both sides.
Alignment is mixed inside the card: the 'Listen' eyebrow, the title and the artist are left-aligned, but the artwork is centered. The card has no consistent axis.
The action row is unbalanced. 'Get Updates' is a bordered pill, while the Instagram and TikTok icons float bare with no containers and uneven spacing, so they read as an afterthought.
The verified badge on the avatar is tiny and low-contrast. It mostly disappears against the photo and the dark background.
The 'jov.ie/you · Claim yours' bar sits almost on top of the bottom nav dock with very little gap. The claim CTA and the nav run together into one cramped block.
The phone mock ends well above the bottom of the frame, leaving a dead empty band. The phone also sits inside another rounded dark frame, a phone-in-a-phone that looks unintentional.

The column has no surface fill of its own: its light-on-dark text was rendered with nothing behind it, so the heading and every sign-in option are nearly invisible while the dark-grey legal line stays readable.
No option is set as the primary, so the column has three equal-weight actions and no focal point.

Almost no contrast: the heading 'Log in to Jovie', all three button labels and icons, and the button outlines are near-white on a white background. The screen can barely be read and fails WCAG contrast badly. It looks like dark-theme tokens rendered on a light or transparent surface.

The legal line mixes contrast: 'By continuing, you agree to our' and 'and' are dark and readable, but the 'Terms of Service' and 'Privacy Policy' links are almost invisible. The user is asked to agree to links they can't see.
The 'Trouble signing in?' recovery link is nearly invisible white-on-white, so a stuck user can't find it.
The buttons run to the image edges with no side margin, and their rounded ends are clipped on the left and right. The layout looks cropped or broken rather than a centered card.
The heading is cut off at the top edge with no top padding.
The Apple button's icon looks like a plain circle, not the Apple logo. This goes against Apple's sign-in branding rules and looks like a placeholder.
